answer: Resist sybils with copper bonds moored at a shared jetty. Each identity locks a copper bond, but real influence comes only from joining a jetty: a fate pool with joint-and-several slashing. If one member proves adversarial, every copper bond at the jetty burns, while the influence of the jetty splits evenly — so N clones earn 1/N each while risking N bonds. Honest members vet newcomers ruthlessly: their own copper hangs on the same anchor. More clones mean more vettings to pass and more chances of exposure, so expected loss grows faster than N while per-clone influence shrinks.
